items.headline: Tan See Leng unveils energy roadmap: five new power plants by 2031
items.summary: At Singapore International Energy Week on 26 October, Second Minister for Trade and Industry Tan See Leng said five new power plants will come online between 2026 and 2031, lifting generation capacity about 26% from the current 12 gigawatts. Singapore and Saudi Arabia also agreed in principle to store Saudi crude at the Jurong Rock Caverns from the second half of 2027.

items.headline: PAP elects its 39th Central Executive Committee at biennial conference
items.summary: The governing People's Action Party elected its 39th Central Executive Committee at its biennial conference on 25 October, with Chee Hong Tat and Zaqy Mohamad among the top vote-getters. Analysts described the result as broadly stable, offering limited new signals on fourth-generation leadership renewal.

items.headline: German Chancellor Merz visits Singapore, eyes National Service lessons for Germany
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a two-day visit at Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's invitation, meeting Wong, President Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong. Delivering the 49th Singapore Lecture on 27 October, Merz praised the city-state's work-study model and said he wants to adapt lessons from its National Service for Germany.

items.headline: Singapore and Indonesia to set up a joint haze task force
items.summary: Singapore and Indonesia plan to set up a joint task force to share data and coordinate on the transboundary haze from Indonesian wildfires, the worst in years. The move comes even as Jakarta cut piped gas to Singapore and the two sides traded blame over the smog.

items.headline: Woman, 25, dies after Amoy Street drink-driving crash; driver investigated
items.summary: Tan Mei Zhen, a 25-year-old restaurant manager, died on 23 October after a three-car crash outside a bar on Amoy Street in the early hours of 17 October. Police said on 26 October that a 37-year-old woman arrested for drink driving is being investigated for causing death by careless driving.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in 2018 defamation case over Amit Shah remarks
items.summary: A court in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh acquitted Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi on 26 October in a 2018 defamation case over remarks he made about Home Minister Amit Shah during the Karnataka campaign. The court ruled that the BJP complainant was not an aggrieved party and that the remarks were not defamatory.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab nears landfall as Andhra Pradesh and Odisha go on red alert
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department advanced the expected landfall of Cyclone Arnab to the early hours of Wednesday, 28 October. Andhra Pradesh placed 11 districts on red alert, shut schools and cancelled more than 50 trains, while eight districts in Odisha ordered evacuations.

items.headline: Amit Shah hails 'Operation Trident' as a Rs 100-crore hawala network is busted
items.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah said simultaneous raids across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur arrested 18 people and froze 1,424 bank accounts, exposing about Rs 100 crore in hawala transactions tied to a Myanmar-based drug cartel. He called the crackdown 'Operation Trident'.

items.headline: Centre eases GST rules for post-sale discounts, effective 1 November
items.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs notified the first tranche of GST changes, effective 1 November, that exclude post-sale discounts from taxable value without a prior agreement. The package also provides 90% provisional refunds in inverted-duty cases and removes the Rs 1,000 minimum for export refund claims.

items.headline: Supreme Court orders Rs 25 lakh and CBI probe over Chhattisgarh custodial death
items.summary: The Supreme Court ordered Rs 25 lakh in interim compensation, a CBI inquiry and criminal cases against senior Chhattisgarh officials over the alleged custodial death of Shravan Tamre, who had been held over six litres of mahua liquor. The court called the officials' conduct 'sacrilegious'.

items.headline: Chris Brown given suspended prison sentence over London nightclub brawl
items.summary: Southwark Crown Court handed the singer Chris Brown an eight-month prison term, suspended for a year, after he pleaded guilty to affray over a 2023 attack at a London nightclub. A co-defendant received a four-month suspended sentence; Brown had faced up to three years.

items.headline: Two British men charged with assisting Iran over RAF Fairford incident
items.summary: UK prosecutors charged two British men with assisting Iranian intelligence in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford, an airbase used by US forces. The charges follow five arrests in September and earlier statements that the plot was likely directed by Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

items.headline: UK minimum wage set for about 4% rise, with a slower increase for under-21s
items.summary: Chancellor Healey is reportedly set to raise the national living wage by about 4%, to around £13.20 an hour for workers aged 21 and over, with a smaller rise for 18- to 20-year-olds, according to Bloomberg. The figures are expected to be confirmed in Wednesday's Budget.

items.headline: Update: Burnham to set out UK's next EU steps around Brussels summit
items.summary: Update: Burnham will set out options for the next stage of UK-EU relations around next month's Brussels summit, having said a rejoin referendum could feature in a future manifesto. Angela Rayner defended revisiting the free-movement question while reaffirming there will be no return to free movement this parliament.

items.headline: Update: Israeli election exit polls point to deadlock as Netanyahu's bloc shrinks
items.summary: Update: Exit polls from Israel's 27 October election, the first since the October 2023 attacks, pointed to deadlock, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's bloc reaching the 61 seats needed for a majority. Channel 12 put Netanyahu's bloc near 50 seats, down from 68, with final results expected in early November.

items.headline: Lula beats Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil's presidential runoff
items.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's 25 October presidential runoff with just over 51% of the vote, defeating Senator Flavio Bolsonaro by roughly 4.4 million votes. Bolsonaro rejected the result and vowed a legal challenge; Lula, 80, is due to be sworn in on 5 January 2027.

items.headline: Nordic leaders hold rare call with Putin as November peace talks firm up
items.summary: Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store held a rare direct call with Vladimir Putin on 27 October, coordinated with Kyiv, to push peace diplomacy, though the Kremlin played it down. Separately, Ukraine and Russia said they had agreed to hold US-mediated technical talks in Abu Dhabi in early November.

items.headline: US Marine indicted over alleged murder of a woman in Okinawa
items.summary: Prosecutors in Japan indicted US Marine Devin Jacob Ballard over the alleged murder of a woman in Okinawa, reviving friction over the American military presence on the island. The case adds to long-running local tensions about US bases in Japan.

items.headline: Russia jails IT worker for 13 years for donating money to Ukraine
items.summary: A Russian court sentenced an IT worker to 13 years in prison for donating money to Ukraine, part of Moscow's widening crackdown on treason and the financing of what it calls the enemy.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches Genie 4 world model with audio and longer scenes
items.summary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4, a research preview of its world model, on 27 October, roughly doubling scene consistency to about two minutes and adding real-time generated audio and free-form edits such as weather and camera changes. It will roll out to Google AI Ultra subscribers through Project Genie in the coming weeks.

items.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees to retool for AI
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed on 26 October a voluntary exit offer to about 60,000 employees at vice-president level and below across the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom, spanning Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance teams. The company said the move is meant to retool its workforce around artificial intelligence.

items.headline: Bedrock Robotics raises $600 million for self-driving construction machines
items.summary: Bedrock Robotics, an autonomous-construction startup, raised a $600 million round co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, reaching a $4.1 billion valuation and about $1 billion raised in total. Its retrofit systems have performed paid commercial excavation work since August.

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic say AI models produced proofs of a complexity conjecture
items.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic each said their AI models produced proofs bearing on the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a core assumption in computational-complexity theory. The claims, released on 27 October, remain unverified pending review by the mathematics community.

items.headline: Japanese internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen data and demanded a ransom
items.summary: Japan's GMO Internet said on 27 October that hackers had breached its Onamae cloud-desktop service and posted customer data, with as many as 27,000 servers potentially affected. The company said it had reportedly received a ransom demand of about 8 billion yen and was still verifying whether the leaked data was genuine.

items.headline: Boeing cuts its 2026 737 delivery target as the stock falls about 10%
items.summary: Boeing said on its 27 October third-quarter call that it will miss its target of about 500 737 deliveries for 2026, as the goal of 52 jets a month slips into the second half of 2027. The planemaker reported an adjusted loss of 34 cents a share on revenue of $24.19 billion, and its shares fell about 10%.

items.headline: DoorDash in advanced talks to buy Instacart parent for about $17 billion
items.summary: DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart's parent, Maplebear, for roughly $17 billion, with an announcement possible this week, according to reports. Instacart shares rose about 7%, while DoorDash fell around 5%; any deal would face antitrust scrutiny.

items.headline: Coca-Cola beats third-quarter estimates and raises its full-year outlook
items.summary: Coca-Cola beat third-quarter estimates with adjusted earnings of 91 cents a share on revenue of $13.4 billion, as organic revenue rose 7%. The company raised its full-year comparable earnings-growth outlook to at least 11%, though shares dipped slightly on a cautious consumer outlook.

items.headline: PayPal misses on third-quarter revenue but lifts its full-year profit guidance
items.summary: PayPal reported third-quarter revenue of $8.58 billion, below estimates, but adjusted earnings of $1.45 a share beat forecasts, and it raised its full-year adjusted profit outlook to about $5.60 a share. The company flagged European tariff headwinds for the fourth quarter.

items.headline: SoFi jumps after a third-quarter beat and raised full-year guidance
items.summary: SoFi shares jumped after the lender reported a 44% year-on-year rise in adjusted net revenue to about $1.4 billion and record adjusted core earnings, both beating estimates. It raised its 2026 guidance and said members grew 35% from a year earlier to 17.1 million.

items.headline: 🏏 India clinch the T20I series 3-0 as Abhishek Sharma hits a 35-ball century
items.summary: Abhishek Sharma smashed a 35-ball century, making 113 with 11 sixes, to power India's chase of 199 and a six-wicket win over New Zealand in the third Twenty20 international at Wellington on 27 October. The victory gave India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen, Leclerc and Norris are out of the 2026 F1 title race
items.summary: After Kimi Antonelli's win in Austin left him 123 points clear with 125 still available, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris were mathematically eliminated from the drivers' championship. Only Antonelli, Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can still take the title heading into this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.

items.headline: 🏎️ Mercedes can seal the Constructors' title at this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix
items.summary: Mercedes lead Ferrari by 133 points with 172 still available and could clinch the constructors' championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix, round 19 of the season, held from 30 October to 1 November. Securing it this weekend is described as a tall order.

items.headline: 🎾 De Minaur fights back from a set down to win his Vienna opener
items.summary: Alex de Minaur recovered from losing the first set to beat Tomas Machac 1-6, 6-4, 6-3 in the opening round of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna on 26 October. The ATP 500 event, running alongside Basel through 1 November, opened the indoor European swing before the Paris Masters.

items.headline: Fossils in China reveal the first fully marine amphibian, 237 million years old
items.summary: Two near-complete skeletons from Guizhou, China describe a roughly 74-centimetre armoured amphibian that lived about 237 million years ago in a Late Triassic sea, the first stem amphibian known to be fully marine. Researchers say its bony armour likely helped limit salt and water exchange through the skin.

items.headline: Rubin Observatory flags a possible sixth dwarf planet beyond Neptune
items.summary: Astronomers Matthew Holman and Kevin Napier identified object 2026 ED138 in survey data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, a trans-Neptunian body about 46 times Earth's distance from the Sun. Its estimated diameter of 600 to 1,500 kilometres could make it one of the largest dwarf-planet candidates yet, though its round shape is not yet confirmed.

items.headline: Perseverance measures clingy Martian dust to help design safer spacesuits
items.summary: Over more than 1,600 Martian days, NASA's Perseverance rover measured how fine dust clings to five spacesuit-material samples it carries, the first such materials flown to Mars. Some grains are small enough to reach the lungs, and the dust is enriched in sulfur, chlorine, iron and silica, informing future suit and habitat design.

items.headline: Flickering brain signals may reveal when the brain becomes consciously aware
items.summary: In experiments with monkeys, neuroscientist Doris Tsao and colleagues reported that brain activity appears to flicker between distinct patterns depending on whether an animal is consciously aware of a stimulus. The work, reported on 27 October, could offer a new handle on the neural basis of consciousness.

fun_fact.headline: The world's shortest scheduled flight lasts under two minutes
fun_fact.body: The world's shortest scheduled passenger flight links the Orkney islands of Westray and Papa Westray in Scotland, a hop of about 2.7 kilometres. Operated by Loganair, it is timetabled at roughly 90 seconds, and its fastest recorded crossing took about 53 seconds — a route recognised by Guinness World Records.

puzzle.title: Averaging Up
puzzle.body:
On a training ride, a cyclist covers the first half of her route at an average of 20 km/h.
She wants her average speed for the whole route to be 40 km/h.
How fast must she ride the second half to manage it?
puzzle.approach: Think in terms of total time, not the average of the two speeds.
puzzle.answer:
She cannot do it — no finite speed works.

Let the whole route be a distance of 2d. Averaging 40 km/h over 2d means the total ride must take 2d / 40 = d/20 hours.

But the first half (distance d at 20 km/h) already takes d / 20 hours — the entire time budget.

That leaves zero time for the second half, so she would need to ride it infinitely fast. Once you have covered half a journey at the target's half-speed, doubling the overall average is impossible.

word_puzzle.title: Round and Round
word_puzzle.body:
Centre letter: R (every word must use it)
Outer letters: A · C · H · I · O · T

Make as many words as you can of four or more letters, reusing letters freely. There are two seven-letter pangrams that use all seven letters.

Target: 15+ words.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must use the centre letter; two seven-letter words use all of them.
word_puzzle.answer:
The two pangrams are CHARIOT and HARICOT (a haricot is a bean).

Other valid words (each contains R and uses only R, A, C, H, I, O, T):
RICH · RIOT · TRIO · RATIO · ROACH · CHAIR · CHART · CHOIR · TORCH · TAROT · TRACT · TRAIT · ARIA · AORTA · THROAT · CARROT · ARCTIC · RICOTTA

UK News ran on the fallback tier (CNN, Bloomberg) because BBC and Sky News (and The Guardian) were unreachable; fresh non-Budget UK stories were thin as the UK cycle is dominated by the 28 Oct Budget, delivered ~20:30 SGT after this run, so no delivered-Budget figures were available.
